title: Cartier boundary on the group saturation of an affine open
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a smooth connected affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $X$ be a normal separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; normal means that each local ring is an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $a:G\times_kX\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product] be an action, meaning that its identity and associativity diagrams commute as morphism identities. Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. For $g\in G(k)$ write $gU$ for its image under the automorphism $a_g:X\to X$, $y\mapsto a(g,y)$. Give $W=\bigcup_{g\in G(k)}gU$ its open subscheme structure. Then $a|_{G\times_kW}$ factors through $W$, and $W$ is normal, separated, of finite type over $k$ and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. There is an effective Cartier divisor $D\hookrightarrow W$ with $|D|=|W|\setminus|U|$: explicitly its quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_D\subseteq\mathcal O_W$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. The divisor may be empty. No integrality, smoothness or quasi-projectivity of $X$ is assumed, and $U$ need not meet every component of $X$.

source.place: Brion, Algebraic group actions on normal varieties, arXiv:1703.09506v3, Section 3.2, proof of Theorem 1 and Proposition 3.3, first proof paragraph (Cartier assertion only, before ampleness). Local PDF WANTED; primary text read online. The extension to disconnected normal schemes is agent-supplied.

proof.text: The translates $gU$ are open: the action identities give mutually inverse morphisms $a_g$ and $a_{g^{-1}}$. Their union $W$ is therefore an open subscheme. If $U$ is empty then $W$ and its divisor are empty; henceforth allow this case by the same constructions. The field spectrum is Noetherian (a field has only the ideals $0,1$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ and $G$ Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], $W$ and $U$ are Noetherian, in particular quasi-compact. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-closed-finite-presentation] (take the closed immersion to be the identity), $W\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact; [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] and [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] make $W$ of finite type over $k$. The latter node also makes products of these finite-type $k$-schemes finite type. The local rings on $W$ equal those on $X$, hence are normal. Its relative diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $X/k$ to $W\times_kW$, so $W/k$ is separated. By [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated], $W$ is also absolutely separated.

source.place: Open-subscheme permanence; morphisms.tex finite-type permanence; preliminary to Brion Section 3.2

proof.text: The equality $hW=W$ holds for every $h\in G(k)$, since $a_h(gU)=(hg)U$. To upgrade this to scheme-level invariance, let $C=a^{-1}(X\setminus W)\cap(G\times_kW)$, a closed subset of the finite-type scheme $G\times_kW$. If nonempty, [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] supplies a closed ambient point in $C$, and [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a) makes its residue field finite over $k$. Since $k$ is algebraically closed, that field is $k$, giving a pair $(h,w)\in G(k)\times W(k)$. But $hw\in W$ by the preceding equality, a contradiction. Thus $C$ is empty. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] the action restricts to $\alpha:G\times_kW\to W$. Its identity and associativity identities follow after composing with the open immersion $W\to X$; that immersion is a monomorphism by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-closed-finite-presentation].

The group $G$ is normal and reduced by [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal], applied to its smooth structure map. Every quasi-compact open of $G$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], and has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. Consequently [lem-sfb-normal-locally-finite-components] makes the irreducible components of $G$ pairwise disjoint and clopen. Connectedness and the identity point force there to be exactly one. This component, with its reduced induced structure, is $G$ itself. The geometric-irreducibility clause of [lem-sfb-group-local-minimal-prime] now shows that $G_K$ is irreducible for every field extension $K/k$.

Write $p:G\times_kW\to W$ for the second projection. The structure morphism $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine: the field spectrum has only the opens $\varnothing$ and itself, with affine inverse images. It is therefore separated and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), and its smoothness gives local finite presentation. Together these are finite presentation. The base-change clauses of [lem-pc-proper-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] show that $p$ is smooth, separated and finitely presented. The morphisms $b(g,y)=(g,gy)$ and $c(g,z)=(g,g^{-1}z)$ are mutually inverse by the action identities, and $\alpha=p\circ b$. Hence $\alpha$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](c). Its separatedness and finite presentation follow as well: the diagonal squares and affine presentations are carried by this isomorphism to those of $p$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3, first proof paragraph; explicit trivialization of the action map

proof.text: Choose any affine open $T\subseteq W$ from [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], and set $Y_T=\alpha^{-1}(T)$ and $V_T=Y_T\cap(G\times_kU)$. The morphism $f_T:Y_T\to T$ is the base change of $\alpha$, hence smooth, separated and finitely presented by the three base-change results in step 4. The base $T$ is normal and locally Noetherian because its stalks are those of $W$ and it is an open of a Noetherian scheme. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $G\times_kU$ is affine. Its action morphism to the absolutely separated $W$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-separated-target-affine-morphism]. Its inverse image of $T$, which is exactly $V_T$, is therefore affine by the definition [pqf-def-affine-morphism].

source.place: Tag 01SG, lemma-affine-permanence, applied to the action restricted to the affine source

proof.text: For any $t\in T$, with residue field $K=\kappa(t)$, the formula $g\mapsto(g,g^{-1}t)$ identifies $(Y_T)_t$ with $G_K$; its inverse is first projection. By step 3 this fibre is irreducible. There is $h\in G(k)$ with $t\in hU$, directly from the definition of $W$ (no closedness of $t$ is required). The canonical $K$-point $t:\operatorname{Spec}K\to W$ then has $h^{-1}t$ in $U$, by the open factorization criterion used in step 2. Thus $(h,h^{-1}t)$ is a $K$-point of $(V_T)_t$. This fibre is a nonempty open in an irreducible fibre, so it is dense: any two nonempty opens in an irreducible space intersect.

source.place: Proposition 3.3, first proof paragraph: the boundary contains no action fibre; explicit fibrewise density

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-affine-boundary-cartier] to $f_T:Y_T\to T$ and the affine open $V_T$. The base is affine normal locally Noetherian, the map is smooth separated of finite presentation, and step 6 verifies density in every fibre. We obtain an effective Cartier divisor $E_T=(Y_T\setminus V_T)_{\mathrm{red}}$ on $Y_T$. This is the smooth-family Cartier criterion, rather than any assertion about ampleness or quasi-projectivity.

source.place: Proposition 3.3, implication (iii) to (i)/(ii), printed pp.6--7; Noetherian Ramanujam--Samuel case

proof.text: Let $D=(W\setminus U)_{\mathrm{red}}$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme furnished by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], with its quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_D$. It is locally Noetherian: its closed immersion is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](c), hence of finite type; composing with $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] and applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] even makes $D$ Noetherian. The projection $G\times_kD\to D$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Since $D$ is reduced, [lem-trf-smooth-reduced-dense-pullback] makes $G\times_kD$ reduced. Its immersion into $G\times_kW$ is closed by base change of $D\hookrightarrow W$, using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b).

source.place: Tags 01J3/01J4, reduced closed structure, and descent.tex Tag 034E, smooth reducedness

proof.text: Put $B=G\times_kD=p^{-1}(D)$ as a closed subscheme. On $Y_T$ its underlying closed set is $Y_T\setminus V_T$, since $D$ has complement $U$. Both $B|_{Y_T}$ and $E_T$ are reduced; uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](3) identifies their ideal sheaves, including their inclusions in $\mathcal O_{Y_T}$. The opens $Y_T$ cover $G\times_kW$ as $T$ runs through the affine opens of $W$. Therefore the actual ideal of $B$ is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor: this holds on each $Y_T$ by step 7. Thus $B\hookrightarrow G\times_kW$ is an effective Cartier divisor. This identifies closed subschemes and ideals, not just supports.

source.place: Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme, uniqueness; local effective Cartier definition

proof.text: The singleton $\{p:G\times_kW\to W\}$ is an fpqc covering in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Indeed $p$ is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. For every affine open $T\subseteq W$, its inverse image $G\times_kT$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], and maps onto $T$: the identity section $t\mapsto(e,t)$ gives a preimage for every $t$. Thus one affine open in the covering source suffices for each affine target open, exactly as required in that definition.

Apply [lem-trf-fpqc-cartier-ideal-reflection] to $D\hookrightarrow W$, its quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_D$, and the fpqc cover $p$. Its pulled-back closed subscheme is exactly $B$, whose ideal is effective Cartier by step 9. The cited result identifies $p^*\mathcal I_D$ with that ideal and concludes that $\mathcal I_D$ itself is an effective Cartier ideal. Hence $D$ is the required effective Cartier divisor with $|D|=|W|\setminus|U|$. The unit ideal is allowed, so this includes $U=W$ and the empty saturation. No component of $X$ omitted by $U$ has been introduced into $W$, and the proof has not assumed that $X$ is integral or smooth.

source.place: Tag 05B2, rank-one descent, retaining the ideal inclusion; conclusion
